title: Seeking Feedback on an AI-Based Swing Trading Research Tool
author: xdrive0513
selftext: I've been developing an AI-assisted stock research platform called Triadent Group. The goal is to identify potential swing-trading opportunities using a systematic, data-driven approach rather than relying solely on manual screening. I've been testing various signal-generation and ranking methods and would love feedback from other traders interested in AI and quantitative research. If anyone is willing to take a look at [Triadent Group](https://triadentgroup.com) and share thoughts on the methodology, user experience, or feature ideas, I'd greatly appreciate it. This is intended as a research and educational tool, not financial advice.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The hard part of any AI swing tool isn't generating signals, it's proving they aren't just curve-fit to the last bull run. What's your out-of-sample setup, walk-forward or just a train/test split? Ranking methods love to look great in backtest and fall apart live, so I'd want to see turnover, slippage assumptions, and how it handles regime shifts. Also worth being honest about what 'systematic' buys you here, most retail swing edges die to costs and bad fills. Cross-checking against independent analysis like the trademates platform or similar screeners can help sanity-check your rankings against something you didn't build. What timeframe and universe are you ranking over?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
one question rather than a review: what does a ranked name look like a month after it was ranked? every research tool shows this week's list; almost none keep the old lists next to what those names did after. if every ranking is stored with its date and the forward result sits on the same page, ugly weeks included, that's the thing that would make me trust the methodology more than any description of it.

I run a free paper desk I built, Quantradin at quantradin.com, and what people come back for is the record of what a rule did after it was written, not the rule itself.
